description: The codes of `ErrorCode` in the API's OpenAPI spec that `error-codes.json` deliberately leaves out: the SDKs answer them with the fallback type for their status. Every code of the spec is either in `error-codes.json` or here, never both — the contract tests of the SDKs hold that in both directions, so a code the backend adds turns them red until somebody decides: a type of its own (error-codes.json plus the table of every SDK) or a line here, under the reason that applies. The rules are in the AGENTS.md of each package.

runtime.reason: Raised behind the endpoints the SDKs call — the reservation lifecycle, the gateway, the flow runtime, the request middleware, the customers API — and left to the fallback on purpose: the type for the status is the right one. A 400, 404, 409 or 422 here is a request to fix (`InvalidRequest`), a 403 is about the key (`Authentication`). The error taxonomy went through this list; the codes whose fallback type was wrong — a 5xx that is not a provider failure — have a row in error-codes.json now. `execution_parked` never reaches the wire: the runtime catches it and answers 202. `reservation_expired` is raised by the capture of a hold inside the runtime, which no route of the SDKs answers with since the SDKs took no holds; `customer_has_history` is the 409 of a delete that should have been a block — a request to fix, `InvalidRequest` by the fallback.

console.reason: Raised by the console and the configuration plane — sign-in and sessions, organizations, members and invites, projects, keys, policies, budgets, alerts, webhooks, provider connections and pools, flow authoring, approvals, notifications (channels, routes, subscriptions, the Telegram bot, the unsubscribe link). No SDK method calls those endpoints, so a type would have nobody to catch it.
